analysis:
Docs-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md; no executable code or controls changed. The visible patch excerpt is truncated, and the head units show only part of the file. I examined both head-text units (lines 364-791 and 792-1178) against the threat model.

The only visible changed lines in the patch are the `sandbox` table row (line ~182), which adds the Darkbloom Sandbox waitlist approval requirement for `sandbox setup`, and an added row around line 191. The new waitlist anchor (#darkbloom-waitlist) and the added content at head lines 1360-1385 and 1635-1727 are not visible in the supplied units, so I could not review them.

The documented security-relevant behavior matches existing controls:
- `logout` revokes the saved token only at its recorded issuer (A-008, T-053).
- It follows no redirects and confirms remote revocation only for HTTP 204.
- It holds the instance lock while revoking and deleting the token.
- `switch` is fenced behind coordinator receipts and fails closed.
- `gpu-limit` requires a terminal, user confirmation and an administrator prompt (TB-014, T-062).
- Model verification and the hash/fingerprint reuse description do not weaken the mandatory fresh and SSD checks.
- The prefix-cache description (T-041) is unchanged.

I found no contradiction with the threat model and no new attack surface. The documentation does not state that the sandbox waitlist approval is enforced client-side. Where it is enforced (service or add-on) is outside the supplied evidence. This is a possible later question for TB-013/T-061, since the waitlist gate does not change installer integrity. The unseen tail of the file, including the waitlist section, should get a quick pass if available.
